mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office, Registrar of Companies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarization by a New Zealand Notary Public where the receiving jurisdiction requires it, followed by Apostille issued by the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs Authentications Unit. Consular Legalization path for non-Apostille states: notarization by New Zealand Notary Public, followed by authentication by the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs, followed by legalization at the Embassy or Consulate of the destination country in New Zealand or Wellington. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive; Apostille and consular legalization are never chained sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding any shareholder, director, UBO, authorised signatory, counterparty, or beneficial owner of the virtual CFO client book, the New Zealand company must perform initial and ongoing adverse media, PEP, and sanctions screening against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the UK HM Treasury consolidated list, the Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade consolidated list, and all New Zealand autonomous and UN-designation sanctions, including the Russia Sanctions Act 2022 and any delegated sanctions regulation. All domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, their family members, and close associates, as defined under the AML/CFT Act, must be subjected to enhanced due diligence, source of wealth and source of funds verification, senior management approval, and transaction monitoring. Screening must be repeated at least on each business day and before any payment, invoice issuance, or change of control, with false positives recorded, cleared, and auditable. This protocol satisfies the Financial Intelligence Unit expectations for a low-risk standard financial services reporting entity.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Companies Register and Business Name Search portal (companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in the Latin alphabet; English and te reo Maori words are acceptable, including correctly spaced macrons only where the underlying alphabet supports standard Unicode New Zealand orthography. Non-Latin scripts such as Chinese characters, Cyrillic, or Arabic must be romanised or phonetically transliterated into a Latin-script representation because the Companies Register does not accept non-Latin characters as a standalone legal name. The four-tier naming convention applied by the Registrar is: (1) uniqueness against existing and reserved names, (2) visual and phonetic distinctness so the proposed name is not almost identical to an existing name, (3) absence of offensive or obscene expressions, and (4) no false or misleading implication of government, Crown, statutory, charitable, trust, banking, insurance, or other regulated status. The word Limited or Ltd must appear as the last element of the company name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Before the initial 20-working-day reservation expires, log into the New Zealand Companies Office online portal and apply for an extension of the name reservation for an additional 20 working days; an extension will not be granted after the proposed company is incorporated. If the Registrar rejects the name, the notice will state the statutory ground under the Companies Act 1993. If the rejection is for a prohibited or sensitive word, obtain and upload the prior written consent of the responsible Ministry or regulator, such as the Reserve Bank of New Zealand, the Financial Markets Authority, the Ministry of Education, or the Ministry of Consumer Affairs. If the rejection is for whether the name is almost identical to an existing or reserved name, file a written request for reconsideration addressed to the Registrar within 10 working days of the refusal, explaining the visual, phonetic, and contextual distinctions and why there is no realistic likelihood of confusion. Maintain a complete client instruction letter and copies of all search reports. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may appeal to the High Court of New Zealand under the Companies Act 1993 judicial review jurisdiction, and legal counsel should annotate the Companies Register file and issue a final adverse decision memorandum.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office in New Zealand will satisfy the Companies Office registered office requirement only if it is a genuine physical street address in New Zealand, staffed and capable of receiving official documents and service of process, and is not merely a post-office box, a document exchange number, or a bare mail-forwarding mailbox. Inland Revenue and New Zealand banks will usually reject a bare commercial mailbox as the company's principal place of business because the AML/CFT business risk assessment requires a physical premises, accessible records, and a substantive management presence. For the outsourced virtual CFO advisory industry, the appropriate structure is a registered office service provider that offers a leased desk or serviced office, a physical New Zealand street address, mail scanning, meeting rooms, and a responsible local agent, combined with documented commercial substance such as a service agreement, a New Zealand resident director or alternate director, local tax registration, and a real principal place of business. Use of a pure virtual address without staff or lease is likely to be rejected by banks for business account opening, may be challenged by Inland Revenue under residence and permanent establishment rules, and could undermine the AML/CFT risk rating. Best practice is to maintain a virtual office only as an overlay to a formal serviced office or executive centre with a local physical presence and full records access.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspection readiness: (i) current lease, license, or virtual office master service agreement for a physical New Zealand address; (ii) presence of the director, local agent, or staff during normal business hours or a documented attendance schedule; (iii) physical signage or directory listing matching the exact registered company name; (iv) electronic and physical books and records accessible at the registered office; (v) a mail handling protocol that separates statutory mail, bank mail, and IRD correspondence; (vi) completed IRD income tax, GST, and FSP registrations where required; and (vii) an AML/CFT compliance programme with the appointed compliance officer's contact details and audit trail. Quantified risk: for a low-risk virtual CFO company with a credible registered office, a New Zealand resident director, a clean tax history, and no employees in New Zealand, the estimated probability of an unannounced physical inspection by Inland Revenue or the Companies Office in the first 24 months after incorporation is 15-20%. That probability increases to approximately 40-50% if the company claims sizeable GST refunds, files late, repeatedly changes directors or registered offices, has no local substance, or triggers financial crime or name-based alerts from government agencies.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), particularly sections 12-16 (Incorporation), 20-21 (Constitution), 122-124 (Directors), 189-190 (Shareholder Meetings), and 201-202 (Financial Reporting)

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Registration Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (online portal: www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the Companies Office register to ensure the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing entity. Reserve the name for up to 20 business days. Prepare and file Form 1 (Application for Registration) electronically, attaching the constitution (if any), consent to act as director forms (Form 2) for each director, and the registered office address. Ensure all directors provide their full legal names, residential addresses, and date of birth. The application must be signed by each director or an authorized agent. Pay the prescribed fee via the online payment gateway. Upon approval, the Companies Office will issue a Certificate of Incorporation with a unique company number.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and reservation receipt
Form 2 (Consent to Act as Director) for each director
Registered office address in New Zealand
Director identification documents (passport or driver's license)
Agent authorization (if using a registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried due to name conflict or incomplete information, the Companies Office will issue a notice of deficiency. The applicant must respond within 20 business days by amending the application or providing additional documentation. If the name is rejected, file a new name reservation. If the application is suspended for non-compliance, seek legal advice to rectify the issue and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) Registration for Tax and GST
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand (online via myIR portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, the company must register for a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) and obtain an IRD number. This is done online through the IRD's myIR system. The company must also register for Goods and Services Tax (GST) if its annual turnover is expected to exceed NZD 60,000, and for employer obligations (PAYE) if it will hire staff. Provide the company's legal name, incorporation number, registered office, and director details. The IRD will issue an IRD number and GST registration certificate. For a virtual CFO service, also register for the Financial Services Provider (FSP) regime if providing financial advice, though this may be exempt under certain conditions.
required_dossiers: Estimated turnover declaration for GST registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD registration is delayed or queried, the company should contact the IRD business helpline or use the myIR messaging system to provide additional information. If the GST registration is rejected due to insufficient turnover, the company can apply for voluntary registration. If the FSP registration is required but not obtained, the company must immediately apply to the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) to avoid penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and AML/CFT Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banks in New Zealand (e.g., ANZ, ASB, BNZ, Westpac) and the Department of Internal Affairs (for AML/CFT supervision)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a bank and schedule a meeting to open a corporate bank account. The bank will require the company's certificate of incorporation, constitution, director and shareholder identification, and a resolution from the board authorizing the account opening. The bank will conduct a customer due diligence (CDD) process under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT). Provide the source of funds and the nature of the business (virtual CFO services). The bank may require a physical presence or a video call for verification. Once the account is opened, the bank will issue account details and online banking credentials. The company must also appoint a compliance officer and adopt an AML/CFT program if it falls under the definition of a financial institution, though virtual CFO services may be exempt if not handling client funds.
required_dossiers: Board resolution authorizing bank account opening
Director and shareholder identification (passport, proof of address)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the application due to insufficient documentation or high-risk jurisdiction, the company should provide additional evidence of the business model and source of funds. If the bank requires a physical presence, the company may use a registered agent or a virtual office address. If the AML/CFT compliance is deemed inadequate, the company must engage a compliance consultant to draft a robust program and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Setup and Statutory Register Maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and the company's own registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, the company must establish its statutory registers, including the share register, director register, and minute book. The board must hold its first meeting and adopt the pro-forma resolution as provided. The company must also file an annual return with the Companies Office each year, and maintain a registered office address. For a virtual CFO service, the company should also register for the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) if it provides financial services as defined under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008, unless an exemption applies. The company must also appoint a dispute resolution scheme if required. Ensure all director and shareholder changes are filed within 20 working days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return is not filed, the Companies Office will issue a reminder and may remove the company from the register. The company must file the return and pay any late fees. If the FSPR registration is required but not obtained, the company must apply immediately to the Financial Markets Authority. If the company fails to maintain proper registers, it may be subject to penalties; the company should rectify the records and file a restoration application if struck off.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand; online electronic portal is myIR at ird.govt.nz
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity must first be established or recognised at the New Zealand Companies Office, then apply to Inland Revenue for an IRD number via the myIR portal. If the entity is not incorporated in New Zealand, it must provide to the IRD certified evidence of foreign incorporation, the constitutional documents and memorandum of association, a completed non-resident company registration application as prescribed by the IRD, the names and tax residence details of all directors and ultimate beneficial owners, and a statement of intended business activities in New Zealand. Upon verification the IRD issues an IRD number which serves as the master tax file number for income tax, GST, PAYE, and other New Zealand tax obligations. The same IRD number is used as the GST registration identifier when the entity registers for GST, whether compulsorily upon breaching the taxable supply threshold or voluntarily.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A New Zealand limited company may make a Look-Through Company (LTC) election under the Income Tax Act 2007 to be treated as a transparent entity for income tax purposes, subject to eligibility requirements including a maximum of five shareholders. A GST grouping election is also available under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 to tax a group of related companies as a single registered person. No check-the-box election equivalent to United States Subchapter S exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 annual taxable supplies; registration is mandatory once turnover exceeds NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period, and is available voluntarily to a business carrying on a taxable activity
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not operate a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital tax stamping regime. E-invoicing using the Peppol BIS 3.0 format is available on a voluntary basis through the IRD-approved network. Taxpayers must retain GST invoices and business records in accordance with the Tax Administration Act 1994, and the IRD may require electronic data exchange in audits, but there is no API-based pre-clearance of invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods, a supply is zero-rated if the goods are exported from New Zealand within the statutory timeframe and the exporter holds sufficient evidence of export as required under section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. For services, zero-rating applies under section 11A when the services are supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand when the services are performed, and the services are not supplied to a person in New Zealand or the appointment is not related to a registered recipient's business in New Zealand. Offshore digital services, including virtual CFO and bookkeeping services, qualify for zero-rating if the recipient is a non-resident and received the services while outside New Zealand.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export entry lodged electronically and approved by the New Zealand Customs Service
Bill of lading or air waybill evidencing physical export from New Zealand
Commercial invoice and contract or purchase order identifying the overseas buyer or non-resident recipient
Bank records or SWIFT MT103 payment confirmation showing foreign exchange receipt from outside New Zealand
Completed GST export evidence checklist if requested by the Inland Revenue Department
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the IRD determines that zero-rating was applied to a supply that did not meet the statutory export or offshore supply criteria, the entity is liable for the unpaid GST at 15%, plus use-of-money interest. Shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 apply for incorrect or abusive tax positions: up to 20% for a lack of reasonable care, up to 40% for gross carelessness, up to 100% for an abusive tax position, and up to 150% for evasion or fraudulent intent. Willful or fraudulent claims may also lead to criminal prosecution, fines, and cancellation of GST registration.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Putea Matua)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a fully open and convertible currency regime. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) floats freely on global markets with no administrative exchange controls, no surrender requirements, and no mandatory central bank approval for cross-border flows. Both current account transactions (trade in services, consultancy fees, interest, dividends) and capital account transactions (foreign direct investment, equity injection, intercompany loans) are liberalised under the OECD Liberalisation Code. There are no restrictions on the repatriation of profits or capital for a standard NZ Ltd, provided the company is not in a sensitive industry subject to the Overseas Investment Act. The only friction points are prudent compliance: banks require a source-of-funds narrative for large inbound transfers, and outbound dividend payments must be supported by board minutes, solvency certification, and an available earnings calculation under the Companies Act. Tax clearance from Inland Revenue may be requested for high-value distributions to non-resident shareholders to ensure the appropriate non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) is deducted at the rate under the applicable double tax agreement. For this fractional CFO advisory business, all service fees earned in foreign currency can be brought onshore without conversion constraints, and the treasury team may retain appropriate working capital in offshore settlement accounts without triggering regulatory penalties. The absence of surrender rules means no forced conversion into NZD, which is ideal for a multicurrency ledger business serving clients across Asia and the Pacific.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender rules exist. Exporters of services or goods are not required to convert foreign exchange earnings into NZD nor to repatriate them within any specific timeline. Companies may hold proceeds in approved foreign currencies in their domestic bank accounts or offshore accounts, subject to the entity's ordinary financial reporting and AML/CFT obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Currency Account with SWIFT access

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High viability for payment collection and disbursement using Wise and Stripe as licensed financial service providers in New Zealand, but these rails cannot replace a regulated tier-1 bank account for statutory capital escrow, certified treasury operations, or regulatory custody. Non-bank EMIs are not subject to the Reserve Bank's prudential regulation as deposit takers and are legally barred from accepting statutory capital deposits or acting as the sole account for entity formation. They may be used as a settlement convenience for international consulting fees, provided the underlying contracts clearly map every inflow to an invoice and the company's NZBN is included on all payment references. Banks will require a reconciliation of all Wise/Stripe transactions to the tier-1 bank ledger, and a legal opinion may be requested if the EMI’s beneficial ownership structure is not transparent. Thus the domestic tier-1 bank remains the treasury anchor; the EMI rail is a compliant add-on rather than a substitute.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a New Zealand company, at least one director must be a New Zealand resident (or an Australian resident who is also a director of a New Zealand company). All tier-1 banks enforce manual or video-verified identity screening. In practice, each Australian/NZ resident director must appear in person at the branch or via a bank-approved videoconference interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not permitted for initial account activation. If no director is resident, a statutory agent (lawyer) with power of attorney can be used, but the bank will undertake a deeper economic-nexus and source-of-wealth review. This should be planned for prior to incorporation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owner with no local operational footprint or physical office
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide certificate of incorporation, registered office certificate, statutory director register, an NZBN extract, a fully executed service agreement with a New Zealand client, the UBO's source of wealth file (e.g., audited financial statements, bank reference, tax returns), and a subscription agreement explaining the capital injection into the NZ entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multicurrency fee receipts from overseas clients without supporting consulting deliverable metadata
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a documented engagement file: signed master service agreement, detailed scope of work, time-track data, monthly management reports, an audit trail of cloud-based accounting entries, and tax invoices issued through a compliant billing platform showing the unique client reference.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of Wise/Stripe as primary payment channels may be mistaken for unlicensed money service business activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the EMI's independent Financial Services Provider registration, its AML/CFT audit certificate in New Zealand, the commercial terms, all platform KYC/KYB records, and a written explanation proving that funds are only used for the company's advisory revenue and external vendor payments, never for third-party onward settlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapidly accumulated undistributed earnings triggering suspicion of dividend stripping or profit shifting
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide historical board minutes approving profit retention, a quarterly cash-flow forecast, evidence of reinvestment into business infrastructure, and a transfer pricing policy prepared in accordance with OECD principles for the intra-group service fee if applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity injections must be wired via SWIFT MT103 quoting 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' in the purpose field and referencing the company's NZBN and incorporation number. A board resolution authorising the share issue and a signed shareholders' report must be delivered to the bank on request. Funds are first credited to the Capital Escrow Account and remain quarantined until the company files the share allotment notice with the Companies Office and obtains a tax-payer identification from Inland Revenue. For service fee income rooted in a recurring client contract, the wire should reference the invoice number and include a direct link to the engagement agreement to ensure the bank does not categorise the inflow as capital. No Reserve Bank approval is required, but the bank may require a bank statement from the remitting institution and a declaration of the source of the funds if the amount exceeds NZD 10,000.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for the virtual CFO advisory business are executed via SWIFT MT103 for standard vendor payments and supplier fees, with purpose codes such as 'PAYMENT FOR SERVICES'. For high-value or contractually sensitive disbursements, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit (SWIFT MT700) may be issued by the NZ corporate bank in favour of the beneficiary, or alternatively a documentary collection (D/P or D/A) may be used to mitigate settlement and freight risk. All outbound wires must be reconciled against the cloud accounting ledger, and any cross-currency conversion must be priced using the bank's treasury desk or a pre-arranged booking via the treasury management system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward FX contracts in NZD/USD and NZD/EUR up to 24 months for foreign receivable hedging
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or illiquid currencies (e.g., VND, PHP, IDR) settled in NZD
Cross-currency swaps on fixed-floating or fixed-fixed basis for notional exchange and interest rate conversion between NZD and functional currencies
Plain-vanilla FX options (calls and puts) to hedge budgeted net exposure with premiums captured in NZD

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of a New Zealand Limited Company (Companies Act 1993, s 208)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing due by the last day of the month following the anniversary month of incorporation (e.g., if incorporated on 15 June, the annual return is due by 31 July every year).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 100 (approximately USD 62.00) if the annual return is filed after the due date. If the annual return remains outstanding for more than 2 consecutive years, the Registrar may issue a strike-off notice and remove the company from the Companies Register, resulting in the company's dissolution and the vesting of its assets in the Crown. Directors may also be subject to personal liability for continuing to trade during delinquency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership Information) Amendment Act 2023, as integrated with the Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same statutory due date as the Annual Return: by the last day of the month following the anniversary month of incorporation. Any change to a significant beneficial owner (holding 25% or more of shares or voting control) must be reported to the Companies Office within 30 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or incomplete UBO information is an offence under the Companies Act 1993, subject to fines up to NZD 10,000 for the company and NZD 5,000 for each director. Persistent failure to provide a UBO confirmation with the annual return automatically triggers the same strike-off sanction applied to the annual return delinquency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Notice of Change of Registered Office, Registered Agent, Director, or Director Address (Companies Act 1993, s 212)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: One-off filing required, not annual, but must be filed within 20 working days of the occurrence of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No specific monetary penalty for late filing, but failure to maintain accurate records may result in original/default fines up to NZD 5,000, and continued non-compliance can be used as evidence for the Registrar to disqualify a director or strike off the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Return of Allotment of Shares (Companies Act 1993, s 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing due within 10 working days after the allotment of shares. This is a rolling event-based filing, not an annual filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may expose the company to a fine of up to NZD 5,000. The Registrar may also require the return to be completed by a statutory notice, and non-compliance can lead to a further action for strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 (New Zealand), a company is legally required to prepare financial statements and obtain a qualified certified auditor's report if it is a 'large' company. A company is 'large' if it triggers any two of the following three quantitative thresholds for each of the two immediately preceding accounting periods: (1) total assets exceed NZD 60 million (approximately USD 37.2 million); (2) total annual revenue exceeds NZD 30 million (approximately USD 18.6 million); (3) 100 or more full-time equivalent employees. Furthermore, any company that carries on a 'financial markets' activity or is otherwise a 'FMC reporting entity' under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 is compulsory audited regardless of size. For a private outsourcing company providing virtual CFO services, the default audit exemption applies unless the company is large or a shareholder or the Registrar demands an audit under section 207 of the Companies Act 1993.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (NZ GAAP). Large companies must apply the full New Zealand equivalents to International Financial Reporting Standards (NZ IFRS). Non-large companies may apply NZ IFRS with Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR) if they do not have public accountability, or the simplified 'Financial Reporting Standards' available to small and medium enterprises (SMEs) under the Financial Reporting Act 2013. The company must also maintain accounting records sufficient to enable the preparation of financial statements in accordance with NZ GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual return to the Companies Office serves as the annual confirmation of direct shareholders. In addition, under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership Information) Amendment Act 2023, every company must maintain a beneficial ownership register and file an annual beneficial ownership confirmation together with the annual return. Any change in beneficial ownership (i.e., any person holding 25% or more of the shares or controlling the company, whether directly or indirectly) must be recorded in the internal beneficial ownership register and reported to the Companies Office within 30 days of the change. The company must take reasonable steps to identify its beneficial owners from all known information and maintain the register for at least 7 years after a person ceases to be a beneficial owner.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000.00 to USD 25,000.00 per external audit engagement for a low-risk private company with the specified ISIC 6920 outsourced CFO activity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Flat 28% corporate rate on net taxable income. No statutory tax holiday regime. Principal preferences: (i) R&D Tax Incentive of 15% on eligible R&D expenditure; (ii) full imputation credit system attaching 28% shareholder tax credits to dividends; (iii) no New Zealand capital gains tax on share disposals; (iv) depreciation, trading stock, and loss-offset facilities; (v) inbound thin capitalisation safe harbour of 60% gearing for non-resident-owned groups.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_note: Indefinite carryforward with no statutory time limit under s IA 4 Income Tax Act 2007; loss utilisation denied if a breach of the 49% shareholder continuity requirement occurs (average voting interests must remain at least 49%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.imputation_regime: The company must operate an Imputation Credit Account (ICA); ICA debit balances at year-end attract 28% resident withholding tax; dividend statements must attach imputation credits; non-resident dividends remain subject to NRWT and may be fully imputed to the extent of the ICA credit.
corporate_income_tax_regime.provisional_tax_framework: Residual income tax above NZD 5,000 triggers provisional tax; standard 31 March balance date instalments due 28 August, 15 January, and 7 May; terminal tax due 7 February (no tax agent extension) or 7 April (tax agent extension).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Income Tax Return filed electronically through the Inland Revenue myIR secure portal or via an approved software provider / tax agent gateway; financial statements summary and IR10-equivalent schedules must be attached; paper filing only with Commissioner approval.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date: IR4 due 7 July immediately following year-end; with an IRD-registered tax agent holding an extension of time, filing is extended to 31 March of the following year. Terminal tax is due 7 February (without extension) or 7 April (with extension); provisional tax instalments fall due 28 August, 15 January, and 7 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross fees from outsourced CFO services, subscription retainers, project-based consulting, and bookkeeping revenue, net of GST zero-rated supplies, recognised on an accrual basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned NZ Ltd must declare all New Zealand-sourced and worldwide revenue; income derived from services performed in or from New Zealand is generally taxable in New Zealand regardless of foreign client location.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross interest received on bank deposits and term investments, with resident withholding tax (RWT) credits disclosed in the tax credits section.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest derived from New Zealand sources is taxable at 28%; foreign bank account interest is also taxable unless a CFC or attribution rule applies; RWT credits on NZ interest are claimed at Box 30.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross dividends received from New Zealand companies with attached imputation credits and from foreign companies; imputation credits and foreign tax credits are separately claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-owned NZ companies declare local and foreign dividends; dividends from CFCs may require attribution rather than inclusion; foreign tax credits are claimed at Box 33.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-trading sundry income, foreign exchange gains, government grants, and recoveries; any amount not classified as trading, interest, dividend, or rental income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All amounts derived from New Zealand sources must be included; non-residents cannot rely on the absence of a New Zealand permanent establishment to exclude income earned through the NZ Ltd.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating costs including contractor fees, SaaS subscriptions, Stripe and Wise transaction charges, bank fees, office overheads, and marketing; capital items are excluded.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border related-party management fees and contractor payments must satisfy arm's length pricing under transfer pricing rules; payments to offshore related parties must be supported by documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible legal, accounting, tax agent, and compliance fees including AML/CFT audit and DIA registration costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Professional fees paid to related offshore service providers are scrutinised for economic substance; absence of invoices or service evidence triggers disallowance and shortfall penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation on fixed assets and amortisation of depreciable intangible assets at prescribed IRD economic rates; notional deductions are prohibited.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Depreciation claimed must reflect New Zealand tax depreciation rates; non-resident owners cannot claim depreciation on assets not economically owned by the NZ entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net profit before taxation after income and expense adjustments; forms the starting point for tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconciliation to taxable income must exclude non-deductible items such as penalties, entertainment restrictions, and non-deductible foreign taxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after loss offsets claimed by the company; used to compute the 28% company tax charge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss offsets require maintenance of the 49% continuity of ownership; any continuity breach eliminates historical loss carryforward.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unabsorbed tax losses of the current year carried forward to future income years subject to continuity; no time limit applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders changing ownership percentage must assess whether continuity is preserved; losses cannot be carried forward across a 51% continuity break.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax at the statutory 28% rate applied to net taxable income before tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 28% flat rate applies to the NZ Ltd as a New Zealand tax resident; no reduced rate applies to foreign-owned entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resident withholding tax credits on NZ interest and dividend income plus RWT on miscellaneous investment income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: RWT credits are only refundable or offsettable against final income tax if the company is the beneficial owner; interposed non-resident conduits are not entitled to refunds under anti-treaty-shopping rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credits attached to dividends received from NZ-resident companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Imputation credits cannot be refunded to non-resident shareholders; they reduce the cash distribution subject to NRWT but are not convertible into a cash refund for foreign investors.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provisional tax instalments paid during the income year via the ratio, estimation, or standard method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Full provisional tax must be paid to avoid use of money interest and late payment penalties; foreign-controlled entities cannot rely on a parent company payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits for foreign income tax paid on foreign-sourced income included in taxable income, subject to the New Zealand foreign tax credit limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign tax credit cap cannot exceed the New Zealand tax payable on the foreign income; excess foreign taxes are not refundable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 34 - Terminal Tax Payable / Refund Due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance of income tax owing after all credits and payments; payment due on the terminal tax date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Terminal tax underpayment triggers use of money interest from the due date; non-resident directors should ensure settlement before departure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory declaration of cross-border related-party transactions exceeding NZD 1 million in aggregate, including loans, service fees, royalties, and cost recharges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Local File must be prepared and made available to IRD within 30 days of request; failure to disclose or maintain the file constitutes a separate compliance offence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: NZD 250 immediately on the due date, plus NZD 50 for each subsequent month or part month, capped at NZD 2,500. Late payment penalties: 1% of the unpaid tax on the due date, plus 2% per month on the outstanding amount. Use of money interest (UOMI) applies to underpayments and terminal tax shortfalls. For deliberate non-disclosure, civil shortfall penalties range from 20% to 100% of the tax shortfall, increased by 50% for obstruction; criminal prosecution may result in fines up to NZD 50,000 and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% NRWT on gross dividends paid to non-residents (Tax Administration Act 1994, Schedule 3). Treaty rates: generally 15% for portfolio holdings and 5% for substantial corporate shareholdings (typically 10% or more of voting power, depending on the DTA, e.g., Australia, United States, United Kingdom, Singapore).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The NZ payer must obtain a valid certificate of residence from the non-resident shareholder before or at the time of distribution, and submit the certificate to Inland Revenue. Practical steps: (i) shareholder provides a completed IR290 Certificate of Residence or a home-jurisdiction tax residence certificate (TRC) endorsed by the foreign tax authority; (ii) NZ company files the IR67 NRWT return and remits NRWT by the 20th day of the month following the dividend; (iii) treaty rate is applied only where the shareholder is the beneficial owner and satisfies any limitation-on-benefits or Principal Purpose Test provision; (iv) for fully imputed dividends, the imputation credit is non-withheld, and NRWT applies to the cash dividend only but the combined effective tax burden cannot exceed the treaty rate; (v) the supplementary dividend election (IR396 style mechanism) allows the company to bear the NRWT on behalf of the foreign parent with a corresponding imputation credit. Certificates must be retained for 7 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory NRWT 15%; treaty-reduced rates commonly 10% (e.g., Australia, Japan, United States); Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% may replace NRWT on interest in respect of NZD-denominated borrowing where the non-resident lender is unassociated and the total NZD debt owed to all non-residents does not exceed NZD 7.5 million in 12 months. Royalties: statutory NRWT 15%; treaty-reduced rates typically 5% to 10% (e.g., Australia 5%, United States 5%, United Kingdom 10%). The reduced treaty rate requires the recipient to be resident in the treaty jurisdiction and beneficially entitled to the income.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File mandatory where the aggregate value of cross-border related-party transactions exceeds NZD 1 million in the income year. Master File mandatory where the aggregate value of cross-border related-party transactions exceeds NZD 10 million in the income year. Safe harbour: cross-border related-party transactions of NZD 1 million or less do not require formal transfer pricing documentation. Low-value intra-group services may be remunerated under the simplified OECD approach. Documentation must be produced to IRD within 30 days of request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not apply Gulf-format Economic Substance Regulations (ESR). Instead, the anti-avoidance framework comprises: (i) the general anti-avoidance rule (s BG 1 and s GA 1 Income Tax Act 2007), which disregards tax avoidance arrangements lacking commercial substance; (ii) OECD/G20 BEPS Action 6 Principal Purpose Test in New Zealand's tax treaties, which denies treaty benefits where obtaining the benefit is a principal purpose; and (iii) substance-over-form and sham doctrines applied by IRD. Indicators of genuine economic substance for the NZ Ltd include: a physical office in New Zealand, substantive board and management decision-making in New Zealand, local employees providing the virtual CFO services, written service contracts, contemporaneous invoicing, and settlement through New Zealand bank and payment processor accounts (Stripe and Wise). A bare parent or conduit company with no employees, no office, and no operational control will be recharacterised and all income attributed to the ultimate beneficial owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Stripe and Wise revenue from the IR4; creating false invoices or fictitious contractor expenses; destroying accounting books and records; claiming fictitious R&D tax credits; filing false IR10 and financial statement attachments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under s 143B Tax Administration Act 1994: fine up to NZD 50,000, plus up to three times the tax shortfall, and imprisonment for up to 5 years; civil shortfall penalty of 100% of the tax shortfall (increased by 50% to 150% for obstruction of investigation); use of money interest accrues from the original due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who direct, consent to, or knowingly participate are personally liable for the company's tax shortfall via the directors' liability regime (ss 155A-156 TAA); director disqualification under ss 283-284 Companies Act 1993; departure prohibition orders enabling IRD to impose travel bans; property freezing and asset preservation orders; extradition proceedings for serious fraud; civil restitution to the Crown in insolvency.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Shell Company Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive management or service fees to an offshore related party or trust to erode New Zealand taxable profit; using a non-arm's length margin on outsourced CFO services; invoicing from a tax-haven entity with no employees or physical presence; failing to prepare a Local File when related-party transactions exceed NZD 1 million; concluding a cross-border loan on non-commercial terms.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing recharacterisation and adjustment under ss GC 13-15 Income Tax Act 2007; shortfall penalty of 20% (unacceptable tax position), 40% (gross carelessness), 50% (abusive tax position), or 100% (evasion); documentation penalties of NZD 20,000 for failure to maintain or provide the Master File or Local File; denial of treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors cannot shelter behind the corporate veil where the arrangement is a sham or mere facade; personal liability for adjusted tax, penalties, and interest; clawback of fees received in insolvency; criminal liability for fraudulent transfer pricing documentation; travel bans and seizure of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the outsourced virtual CFO and bookkeeping practice without registering as a reporting entity with the Department of Internal Affairs; failing to appoint an AML compliance officer; inadequate customer due diligence on foreign clients; failure to verify beneficial owners of client entities; failure to file suspicious transaction reports where client funds routed through Stripe or Wise indicate money laundering; providing CFO services that manage client money without a financial advice or accounting licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil pecuniary penalties under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009: up to NZD 2,000,000 for a company and NZD 300,000 for an individual director for serious non-compliance; criminal money laundering offences under s 243 Crimes Act 1961: imprisonment up to 7 years and/or a fine up to NZD 300,000; suspension or deregistration of the reporting entity; DIA compliance orders with audit costs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors must ensure the reporting entity implements an effective risk assessment and compliance programme; personal penalties of up to NZD 300,000; imprisonment for knowingly permitting client money laundering; disqualification from providing financial or accounting services; extradition and travel bans for cross-border laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: NRWT Repatriation and Unauthorised Treaty Relief
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to a non-resident shareholder without withholding 30% NRWT; applying a reduced treaty rate without obtaining a valid Certificate of Residence or TRC; paying interest or royalties to a related non-resident without NRWT; classifying distributions as loans or service fees to avoid withholding; failing to file the IR67 NRWT return by the 20th of the following month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Personal liability of the company for the full 30% NRWT not withheld; use of money interest from the dividend payment date; late payment penalties of 1% plus 2% monthly; shortfall penalties of 20% to 100% for deliberate avoidance; denial of the dividend deduction in the shareholder's jurisdiction; reassessment of the distribution as a taxable dividend with penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorise an unlawful distribution without NRWT are jointly and severally liable under the TAA directors' liability regime; recovery action against personal assets; disqualification for breach of Companies Act 1993 dividend provisions; criminal prosecution for aiding tax evasion by the non-resident owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Phoenix Company, Reckless Trading, and Residual Tax Debt
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incurring GST, PAYE, and income tax liabilities while insolvent, then deliberately liquidating the NZ Ltd and continuing the same virtual CFO business through a new company to escape tax debts; stripping assets to an offshore trust; failing to file the IR4 and financial statements; issuing a share buyback to a non-resident shareholder while tax obligations remain unpaid.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Personal liability order against directors for unpaid PAYE, GST, FBT, and RWT under ss 155A-156 TAA; illegal dividends void and recoverable; voidable transactions clawed back by the liquidator; penalties of 100% of the shortfall; use of money interest; permanent director disqualification under the Companies Act 1993; Companies Office prohibition on managing companies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face civil restitution to the Commissioner for the entire unpaid tax, plus penalties and interest; reckless trading liability under s 135 Companies Act 1993 for losses to creditors; travel bans through departure prohibition orders until the tax debt is secured; imprisonment for contempt where asset stripping is designed to defeat the Commissioner.
